subject: C++ compilation error when changing prior from exponential to cauchy

messages.author: b66ddf60e652f73b
messages.subject: C++ compilation error when changing prior from exponential to cauchy
parts:
I am running Rstan 2.10.0 on OS X 10.11.6 and I am attempting to change my prior for a parameter (sigma: it is part of cholesky decomposition for varying intercepts on the parameters in a multinomial time series model) from:

   sigma ~ exponential(2) 
to 
   sigma ~ cauchy(0,2.5)

However I get the following error message, which I thought was a C++ compilation error:

Error in if (nchar(CXX) == 0) { : argument is of length zero

In addition: Warning message:

running command ''/Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Resources/bin/R' CMD config CXX 2>/dev/null' had status 69 


This also happens if I change the prior to an exponential(1), exponential(5), or any other cauchy value.


Is this likely a problem in my C++ compiler, a weird bug, or something else?


Below is  prior code block from model:


    //priors

    lambda ~ exponential(1);

    mu ~ normal(0,1);

    sigma ~ exponential(2);

    to_vector(zed) ~ normal(0,1);

    L_Rho ~ lkj_corr_cholesky(3);


And parameter specifications from model:


   parameters {

       real<lower=0> lambda;                   // mutlinomial error parameter

       vector[N_effects] mu;                   // average effects

       matrix[N_effects,J] zed;                // individual z-scores

       cholesky_factor_corr[N_effects] L_Rho;  // correlation matrix

       vector<lower=0>[N_effects] sigma;       // standard deviations

   }

   transformed parameters{

       matrix[J,N_effects] a_id;

       // put scales and correlations back in

       a_id <- (diag_pre_multiply(sigma,L_Rho) * zed)';

   }


Thanks.

messages.author: b66ddf60e652f73b
